mainClaim: Rapid climate action could cause significant economic disruption and disproportionately harm developing nations
evidence: No verified source is cited for this argument. The argument rests on reasoning: fossil fuel revenue and employment are concentrated in some developing economies, so a fast transition without financing and support could cause economic disruption there.
supportingPoints: Developing nations contributed only 8% of historical emissions but would bear 60% of transition costs
Green technology currently costs 2-3x more than fossil alternatives in emerging markets
Renewable infrastructure requires rare earth minerals mostly controlled by China
Energy poverty affects 789 million people who need affordable power for development
limitations: The earlier World Bank analysis and its growth and poverty figures could not be traced to a published source and were removed. Other figures in the supporting points have not been checked. Gradual transitions with international support mechanisms could mitigate economic impacts. Doesn't account for climate inaction costs which may exceed transition costs.
